about: Additions to bridge-contract.json that work both ways, so they do not feed its hash and keep the bridge id (ios/architecture.md D3, D14). Two kinds only. An optional trailing argument: an app built before it sends one fewer, and the engine must answer as it did before when the argument is undefined. An optional return field: an engine built before it leaves it out, and the app must read its absence as none; an app built before it ignores a field it does not know. Anything else, or anything an older app cannot do without, belongs in bridge-contract.json and is a new bridge. bridge.test.ts and EngineBridgeContractTests.swift count each door's arity as its contract args plus these; bridge.test.ts also checks each optional argument trails the contract ones by name and that a call with only the contract args answers as one with them undefined. An optional return field's absence is tested per feature (US-61: USProductsTests). A real bridge change never goes here.

historyJson.optionalReturns: rows[].bound and rows[].note (US-12 AC20): a lab result printed as a limit carries bound, its number in the row's unit, and its value reads "> 60"; the chart plots it at bound, hollow and out of the line. note is the plan's word on an active limit the shared rule (row-grade.ts limitUngraded) leaves ungraded, shown in place of "Used in your plan"; since US-12 AC21 also on weight, waist and blood pressure rows. An engine before them sends neither, so the app draws every point from value as before; an app before them finds no number in a limit's value, so it leaves that point off the chart and still lists it with its symbol. Also, for series "lab" (US-25 AC25): metric is a lab test's series key and the answer is that test's history (labHistory), the same shape; rows[].unit and units are present only for a series reported in more than one unit, so the page lists each row's unit and draws no chart. An engine before it takes no series and answers a lab key as no core metric (the read fails), so the app shows no history; an app before it sends none.

screenJson.optionalReturns: plan.usProducts: us-products.ts's usProductSections, the [PlanSection] ready to draw, for isUS true (the App Store storefront USA) and a known adult: on the Supplements section each product card's suggestion carries usProduct {product, name, line, url} and its US description and references, and the section carries ownershipLine. Left out when no block shows (US-61). An app before it sends no isUS, so it gets none; an engine before it sends no usProducts, so the app draws the plain sections. Its first shape (2026-10-31, {blocks, ownershipLine}) was read by no shipped app, so the change is safe for builds 3 and 4. Also myData.vitals[], bloodTests[] and psa rows' target (health-core rowTarget(...).bare, or null) and previous (the newest earlier day's value in the row's units, or null), US-62 AC8/AC9: an engine before them sends neither, and the app draws the row with its date alone and no bracketed value; an app before them ignores both. Also every such row's status (health-core row-grade.ts valueStatus or pressureStatus: "ok", "warn", "bad" or null) and gradeWords (gradeWords: the words a screen reader says after an off-target value, or null), US-62 AC8 / US-25 AC17, and myData.labTests, the lab tests beyond the core ones as rows of the same shape (lab-series.ts groupLabValues, the web's MyDataRows.tsx labRows): an engine before them sends none, and the app draws every value plain, speaks no grade and lists no lab test row; an app before them ignores all three. Also every such row's note (US-12 AC21): "Printed as a limit, so the plan cannot grade it against its cutoff." for a latest value printed as a limit the rule leaves ungraded, else null, which the app says where the grade would be; an engine before it sends none, and the app says nothing there; an app before it ignores it.

chatEditsJson.optionalReturns: review.seen: opaque JSON, what the record held for each review line (US-67 AC3). The app passes it back as `seen` on the review part's chatEdits edit, and the engine refuses that Save when the record has changed since. An engine before it sends none, and the app sends no seen; an edit without seen saves as before. Also medications.refusal (string or null; with a refusal, lines is [] and undo is null): the reply's medication change could not be read, so nothing is saved and the app says so. An engine before it sends medications null instead, and an app before it ignores the field.
